entries.notes: Preserves stock node, context, executor, message, and entity identity; completes a same-handle C++ serialized publish to a stock subscription and reports both routes.

entries.api: RCLCPPYY_ENABLE_HOOK=1 with an installed startup hook
entries.notes: A fresh interpreter proves startup activation and the C++ publisher route. Node identity remains stock, while executor and Future wrappers preserve stock call signatures and report Python authority.

entries.api: Installed startup hook with RCLCPPYY_ENABLE_HOOK unset or not 1
entries.notes: Fresh interpreters remain on unmodified stock behavior.

entries.api: enable_cpp_acceleration() after rclpy or message modules are imported
entries.notes: The original Node, Publisher, executor, and Future classes are patched in place and message classes are not replaced. Function aliases captured from the rclpy module before activation retain stock behavior but are not instrumented; overridden subclass methods remain user-owned.
Returns the exact stock Node. The custom Context, namespace, remaps, parameters, graph identity, and teardown are covered by the differential contract.
Direct construction and get_name are tested; broader Node behavior is covered by individual entries.

entries.api: Node name/namespace and endpoint identity observed through the ROS graph
entries.notes: Activated and stock scenarios expose the same single requested node and endpoint identity; no companion node is created.

entries.api: Existing subclasses of a Node alias imported before activation
entries.notes: The application corpus constructs an exact pre-activation subclass, preserves its base and Context, and exercises inherited routed methods. Methods explicitly overridden by an application remain application-owned.
Generated message classes remain the original Python classes with unchanged identity and constructor behavior in compatible mode.

entries.api: Nested messages and primitive sequences on the unpatched-message native rclcpp path
entries.notes: The reusable native path has recursive conversion and sequence coverage; transparent import-hook identity for these shapes is not implied.

entries.api: Generated service and action class import redirection
entries.notes: Compatible mode does not redirect generated imports, so stock service/action types remain available. Service types are covered by the application corpus; a full action contract remains open.
Creation, QoS ownership, graph endpoint, and destruction remain stock; publish uses C++ serialization over the same native handle and completes an ordered round trip.

entries.api: Publisher callback_group, event_callbacks, qos_overriding_options, and publisher_class
entries.notes: The application corpus covers a custom publisher class, callback group, explicit QoS, empty event callbacks, and an empty QoS override set. Non-empty event and override behavior remains open.
The complete subscription entity and Python callback dispatch remain stock; ordered delivery and visible backend fallback are covered.

entries.api: Subscription callback_group, event_callbacks, qos_overriding_options, raw mode, and content filters
entries.notes: The application corpus covers callback groups, explicit QoS, empty event callbacks and overrides, raw=false, and no content filter. Raw delivery, active filters, and non-empty event/override behavior remain open.

Stock timer authority is explicit. The corpus covers callback groups, autostart=false, reset, callback execution, cancellation, exception propagation, and destruction; required_cpp rejects before creation.

The stock executor remains authoritative and is reported as Python. Timer servicing, Context shutdown, signature preservation, and required_cpp rejection before spinning are covered; signal handling remains open.

The wrapper delegates to stock execution and reports Python authority. Timer, guard, service, simulated-time, custom executor, callback-exception, signature, and required_cpp fail-before-spin behavior are covered.

entries.api: Custom executors, MultiThreadedExecutor, callback groups, and waitables
entries.notes: A two-thread MultiThreadedExecutor with a reentrant callback group, shutdown, status reporting, and required_cpp rejection is covered. Custom executor subclasses, waitables, and sustained stress remain open.

Future completion remains stock-authoritative under every policy to avoid destabilizing executor internals. Result completion, done callbacks, signature preservation, and required_cpp behavior are covered.
Stock guard-condition identity, callback groups, trigger/dispatch, destruction, compatible status, bounded warnings, signature preservation, and required_cpp rejection before creation are covered.

A local SetBool client/server request, Future response, callback group, discovery, status, identity, and teardown match stock. required_cpp rejects user service/client creation before side effects while preserving constructor-owned services.
Action classes and executors are unmodified stock rclpy. A full goal/cancel/result/feedback differential contract remains open.

entries.api: Local parameter declaration, callbacks, mutation, listing, and parameter-service graph
entries.notes: The stock node remains sole owner. Values, overrides, callbacks, mutation, listing, service graph identity, status, custom Context, and required_cpp rejection before mutation are covered.
Constructor-owned parameter services remain stock-compatible, but remote client calls and parameter-event delivery do not yet have a dedicated differential corpus.
Lifecycle classes and transition services are unmodified stock rclpy. Transition and teardown differential coverage remains open.

entries.api: Normal interpreter exit after rclcpp bringup and node creation
entries.notes: Both the native lane and compatible stock-authority scenario return normally without forced exit, leaked graph identity, or teardown fault.

entries.api: Repeated init/shutdown cycles and multiple contexts
entries.notes: No differential lifecycle matrix currently proves this behavior.

entries.api: C++ message CDR serialization compared with rclpy.serialization
entries.notes: Flat and tested message bytes match the stock serializer; this is a native capability and not yet a global rclpy.serialization patch.
